summary: The paper establishes definitive exact algebraic-combinatorial theorems separating the Shannon capacity Theta(G), the characteristic-p Haemers minrank bound, real shifted-adjacency rank, and Lovasz/Schrijver SDP bounds across strongly regular graphs, polar graphs, Kneser graphs, and sporadic structures such as the Higman-Sims graph. Highlights include universal SRG Schrijver-Lovasz collapse via a primal-dual squeeze, an exact characteristic-p shifted adjacency collapse dichotomy for Kneser graphs KG(m,2) governed by divisibility p|(m-4), exact ternary polar exponential hierarchies and discriminant-parity barriers, and zero-float Sturm-certified primal Schrijver lower bounds. All 20 main theorems are fully formalized in Lean 4 without sorries or Classical.choice, backed by verified SHA-256 certificates and explicit Brouwer-van Eijl (1992) / Peeters (1996) citations.
strengths: Complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization with zero sorries and zero Classical.choice.
Proves universal Schrijver-Lovasz collapse for all strongly regular graphs via a primal-dual squeeze.
Uncovers a sharp characteristic-p divisibility dichotomy (p | m-4) for shifted-adjacency collapse on Kneser graphs KG(m,2).
Establishes precise exponential separations and discriminant-parity barriers on ternary and binary polar graphs.
Extensive cryptographic and programmatic verification artifacts (16 SHA-256 certificates, 56 pytest checks).
weaknesses: Dense algebraic development requires advanced background in extremal graph theory, coding theory, and formal theorem proving.
Computationally intensive verification artifacts require specific Python/Lean toolchains to re-run from scratch (though fully archived).
